label: August 24–30
title: “I Will Declare What He Hath Done for My Soul” —  Psalms 49–51; 61

items.text: The writers of the Psalms shared deeply personal feelings, writing about discouragement, fear, and remorse, sometimes even feeling abandoned by God. If you’ve felt that way, reading the Psalms can help you know you are not alone. They also praise God’s goodness, power, and mercy, reminding us He is ready to forgive.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: We are burdened by evil and sin, but the Lord is good and ready to forgive. Having faith in the Lord doesn’t mean you’ll never struggle with anxiety, sin, or fear. It means you know who to turn to when you do.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The message of Psalm 49 is for everyone, rich or poor. It reminds us that true redemption comes only through Jesus Christ. Ponder how your life is influenced by your testimony that God will redeem your soul from the power of the grave.

Because of the Savior’s mercy, I can be forgiven. King David’s Psalm 51 recognizes our desperate need for forgiveness. Searching this psalm offers hope for finding it. Repentance involves faith that Jesus Christ can and will cleanse us.
To repent, we need faith not only that Jesus Christ can cleanse us but also that He will. Psalm 86:5, 13, and 15 help us know the Savior is both able and willing to forgive our sins.

My testimony of Jesus Christ can help others come unto Him. Ponder how you gained your testimony, and then think about how you can invite others to “come and see the works of God.” Share what the Lord has done for your soul.

It means to “talk of His righteousness all the day long” by sharing your faith and the blessings you have received. Your testimony can be a powerful invitation for others to learn about and come unto Jesus Christ.

The Lord will help me in my time of need. When feeling distant from God, remember His past works and wonders. This remembrance can bring reassurance and help you set your hope in God, knowing He is there for you.

When you are distressed, remembering the works of the Lord and His wonders of old can bring you comfort. These ancient miracles and His promises serve as powerful reminders that He is with us in our struggles.

The psalmists praised the Lord for His goodness, marveled at His power, and rejoiced in His mercy. They understood that while we are burdened by sin, the Lord is good and ready to forgive, offering us a path to redemption.
